name: Marie Curie
branch: While examining pitchblende, Curie found radioactivity stronger than uranium alone could explain.
discovery: Discovery of polonium and radium; foundational work on radioactivity.
struggle: Limited access to education, gender barriers, poor lab conditions and dangerous radiation exposure.
impact: Radioactivity reshaped physics, chemistry, medicine and cancer treatment.
keywords: radioactivity polonium radium pitchblende chemistry physics cancer radiation

name: Rosalind Franklin
branch: X-ray diffraction images captured crucial structural evidence about DNA.
discovery: Photo 51 and related DNA analysis helped reveal the double-helix structure.
struggle: Under-recognition, contested credit and a difficult institutional environment.
impact: Her evidence became part of the foundation of modern genetics and molecular biology.
keywords: dna x-ray diffraction photo 51 double helix genetics molecular biology

name: Katherine Johnson
branch: Hand-calculated trajectories for America’s early human spaceflights.
discovery: Trajectory calculations for Alan Shepard, John Glenn and Apollo-era missions.
struggle: Worked through racial segregation, sexism and the invisibility of “human computers”.
impact: Her calculations helped make crewed American spaceflight safer and more precise.
keywords: nasa orbit trajectory alan shepard john glenn apollo mathematics space human computer

name: Chien-Shiung Wu
branch: Designed the cobalt-60 experiment that tested whether parity is conserved in beta decay.
discovery: Experimental proof that parity is not conserved in weak interactions.
struggle: Faced sexism, racism and Nobel-era under-recognition despite decisive experimental work.
impact: The Wu experiment reshaped particle physics and our understanding of symmetry.
keywords: parity beta decay cobalt nuclear physics weak interaction symmetry wu experiment

name: Tu Youyou
branch: Studied traditional medical texts and tested sweet wormwood extracts scientifically.
discovery: Artemisinin-based treatment for malaria.
struggle: Worked under intense public-health pressure with delayed international recognition.
impact: Artemisinin therapies improved and saved millions of lives worldwide.
keywords: malaria artemisinin sweet wormwood medicine public health parasites

name: Katalin Karikó
branch: Found that modified RNA building blocks could reduce unwanted inflammatory reactions.
discovery: Nucleoside base modifications that helped enable effective mRNA vaccines.
struggle: Years of scepticism, funding difficulty and career setbacks before recognition.
impact: Her work helped make rapid mRNA vaccine development possible.
keywords: mrna vaccine covid nucleoside base modifications biochemistry immunology rna

name: Donna Strickland
branch: Created a way to amplify ultrashort laser pulses without destroying the amplifier.
discovery: Chirped pulse amplification for high-intensity lasers.
struggle: Long-delayed recognition in a field where women were historically underrepresented.
impact: CPA became essential for high-intensity lasers, including uses in eye surgery.
keywords: laser chirped pulse amplification cpa physics optics eye surgery

name: Jocelyn Bell Burnell
branch: Spotted a repeating radio signal while analysing telescope chart recordings as a graduate student.
discovery: Discovery of pulsars: rapidly rotating neutron stars emitting regular radio pulses.
struggle: Her role was widely discussed after the Nobel Prize went to senior male colleagues.
impact: Pulsars became powerful tools for astrophysics, gravity research and cosmic timing.
keywords: pulsars radio astronomy astrophysics neutron stars cambridge telescope

name: Gerty Cori
branch: Explained how the body converts muscle lactic acid into liver glycogen and back into usable glucose.
discovery: The Cori cycle and key mechanisms of glycogen metabolism.
struggle: Worked on less favourable terms than her husband and faced slow academic recognition.
impact: Her work transformed understanding of energy metabolism and diabetes-related biochemistry.
keywords: gerty cori cori cycle glycogen metabolism glucose lactic acid biochemistry

name: Barbara McClintock
branch: Studied maize chromosomes and saw that genetic elements could move position.
discovery: Mobile genetic elements, often called “jumping genes”.
struggle: Her radical discovery was misunderstood and underappreciated for decades.
impact: Transposable elements became central to modern genetics, genome regulation and evolution.
keywords: barbara mcclintock jumping genes mobile genetic elements transposons maize genetics

name: Dorothy Hodgkin
branch: Used X-ray crystallography to determine the structures of large biochemical molecules.
discovery: Structures of penicillin and vitamin B12, later work on insulin.
struggle: Faced gender barriers in employment and worked through severe rheumatoid arthritis.
impact: Her structural work accelerated drug development and molecular biology.
keywords: dorothy hodgkin x-ray crystallography penicillin vitamin b12 insulin chemistry

name: Rita Levi-Montalcini
branch: Studied nerve development in improvised conditions and later identified a signal driving nerve growth.
discovery: Co-discovery of nerve growth factor.
struggle: As a Jewish scientist in Fascist Italy, she was pushed out of formal academic work.
impact: Growth-factor biology opened new ways to understand development, degeneration and disease.
keywords: rita levi-montalcini nerve growth factor ngf neuroscience neurobiology fascist italy

name: Ada Yonath
branch: Pursued the seemingly impossible task of mapping the ribosome’s structure.
discovery: High-resolution ribosome structure through X-ray crystallography.
struggle: Faced scepticism that the ribosome was too complex to map.
impact: Her work improved understanding of protein synthesis and antibiotic action.
keywords: ada yonath ribosome structure x-ray crystallography antibiotics structural biology

name: Elizabeth Blackburn
branch: Mapped telomere biology and helped identify the enzyme that maintains chromosome ends.
discovery: Telomeres and telomerase mechanisms.
struggle: Worked in a field where ageing, cancer and chromosome biology were complex and contested.
impact: Her discoveries transformed research on ageing, cancer and chromosome maintenance.
keywords: elizabeth blackburn telomeres telomerase chromosome ends ageing cancer molecular biology

name: Emmanuelle Charpentier
branch: Helped turn a bacterial immune mechanism into a programmable genome-editing tool.
discovery: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing method with Jennifer Doudna.
struggle: Worked across institutions and disciplines before CRISPR’s importance was widely recognised.
impact: CRISPR changed biological research, medicine, agriculture and genetic engineering.
keywords: emmanuelle charpentier crispr cas9 genome editing genetics bacteria tracrRNA

name: Jennifer Doudna
branch: Used RNA expertise to simplify CRISPR into a precise genome-editing system.
discovery: CRISPR-Cas9 as a general method for genome editing.
struggle: Had to navigate scientific uncertainty, ethical concerns and intense patent disputes around CRISPR.
impact: Her work helped create one of the most powerful tools in modern biology.
keywords: jennifer doudna crispr cas9 genome editing rna molecular biology genetics

name: Janaki Ammal
branch: Used cytogenetics and plant breeding to improve sugarcane suited to Indian conditions.
discovery: Hybrid sugarcane research and chromosome studies across cultivated plants.
struggle: Faced caste, gender and colonial-era barriers in scientific recognition.
impact: Her work strengthened Indian agriculture and helped protect botanical biodiversity.
keywords: janaki ammal botany cytogenetics sugarcane india plants chromosomes silent valley

name: Wangari Maathai
branch: Founded a grassroots tree-planting movement to fight deforestation and community decline.
discovery: A practical ecological model linking trees, women’s livelihoods, democracy and conservation.
struggle: Faced political repression, gendered hostility and resistance to environmental activism.
impact: The Green Belt Movement helped plant tens of millions of trees and shaped global eco-justice.
keywords: wangari maathai green belt movement kenya environment trees sustainable development ecology

name: Maryam Mirzakhani
branch: Connected geometry, topology and dynamical systems through deep work on curved surfaces.
discovery: New understanding of Riemann surfaces, moduli spaces and geometric dynamics.
struggle: Worked in a highly male-dominated field and became the first woman to win the Fields Medal.
impact: Her work changed modern geometry and became a global symbol for women in mathematics.
keywords: maryam mirzakhani fields medal geometry dynamics riemann surfaces moduli spaces mathematics iran

name: Ynes Mexia
branch: Began botanical fieldwork in her fifties and travelled across the Americas collecting plants.
discovery: Collected more than 145,000 specimens and helped document hundreds of plants.
struggle: Challenged sexism, racism, ageism and the claim that women could not travel alone for field science.
impact: Her collections strengthened botanical knowledge of the Americas and conservation history.
keywords: ynes mexia botany mexico latin america plant collector specimens conservation field science
